characters.name: John Jasper
characters.description: Choir-master / orchestra leader at Cloisterham Cathedral; uncle of Edwin Drood; brooding, devoted, and obsessed with the mystery surrounding his nephew.

characters.name: Edwin Drood
characters.description: Young heir and pupil (aspiring engineer); betrothed to Rosa Bud; last seen in Cloisterham before his mysterious disappearance.

characters.name: Rosa Bud
characters.description: Miss Rosa Bud (called Pussy or Rosebud), a young pupil at the Nuns' House; Edwin Drood's fiancée and a central female figure in the narrative.

characters.name: Reverend Septimus Crisparkle
characters.description: Minor Canon of Cloisterham Cathedral; kindly, conscientious clergyman who tutors and protects Neville Landless and acts as moral adviser to others.

characters.name: Mr. Tope
characters.description: Chief Verger of the Cathedral (showman figure); husband of Mrs. Tope; runs certain day-to-day duties and interacts with cathedral characters.

characters.name: Mrs. Tope
characters.description: Verger's wife; a robust, practical woman who works at the Nuns' House and interacts familiarly with pupils and local people.

characters.name: Thomas Sapsea
characters.description: Auctioneer of Cloisterham, later Mayor; prosperous, pompous, and self-important local figure who prides himself on worldly knowledge.

characters.name: Durdles
characters.description: Stonemason and monumental sculptor (called Stony Durdles); an eccentric, often drunk local who knows the Cathedral crypts and graves intimately.

characters.name: Deputy
characters.description: A hideous small boy who follows and stones objects and people (employed or associated with Durdles); an often-mentioned local urchin.

characters.name: Luke Honeythunder
characters.description: A loud, bombastic London philanthropist and professor of philanthropy; energetic and domineering in public philanthropic causes.

characters.name: Neville Landless
characters.description: Young man from Ceylon, twin brother of Helena Landless; impulsive, hot-tempered, taken in by Mr. Crisparkle for education and suspected (then released) in Edwin Drood's disappearance.

characters.name: Helena Landless
characters.description: Sister of Neville Landless; a strong, proud, and sympathetic young woman who befriends Rosa Bud and seeks to protect her brother.

characters.name: Miss Twinkleton
characters.description: Headmistress of the Nuns' House (school for young ladies); affected, theatrical in private, and proprietor of the seminary where Rosa studies.

characters.name: Mrs. Tisher
characters.description: Companion to Miss Twinkleton; a deferential widow who helps look after the pupils' wardrobes and rooms at the Nuns' House.

characters.name: Mr. Grewgious
characters.description: Hiram Grewgious, a careful, angular, respectable solicitor/receiver; guardian of Rosa Bud and a cautious, practical protector.

characters.name: Bazzard
characters.description: Mr. Grewgious's clerk; a pale, discontented subordinate who aspires to literary things (writes plays) and is attached to his employer.

characters.name: Mr. Tartar
characters.description: Former naval officer ('Tartar'), now a cheerful, resourceful London lodger who becomes Rosa's ally and offers rooms and a rooftop garden for secret meetings.

characters.name: Lobley
characters.description: Lobley, man/boatman in Mr. Tartar's employ; assists in rowing and looking after the small boat.

characters.name: Mr. Peartree
characters.description: A member of the Eight Club and a surgeon (member of Royal College of Surgeons); rough-spoken and opinionated.

characters.name: Kimber
characters.description: A dancing-master, member of the Eight Club; sells off by auction and is a local, comparatively trivial, figure in a club discussion.

characters.name: Mrs. Billickin
characters.description: Proprietor/landlady of lodging-rooms (Billickin) in Bloomsbury; candid, businesslike, and blunt about rooms, stairs, and damp.

characters.name: Mrs. Sapsea (EtheLinda)
characters.description: The late Mrs. Sapsea (EtheLinda), referred to in Mr. Sapsea's inscription and mourned in narrative; wife of Mr. Thomas Sapsea (deceased).

characters.name: the Dean
characters.description: The Dean of the Cathedral (unnamed); a venerable clerical figure who interacts with the Chapter and Minor Canon.

characters.name: Mrs. Dean
characters.description: Mrs. Dean, wife of the Dean; referenced as part of the Dean's household.

characters.name: Miss Dean
characters.description: Miss Dean, daughter (or female relative) in the Dean's household; part of the cathedral household referenced in residence.

characters.name: the Chinaman
characters.description: Unnamed Chinaman encountered in the opium den in Cloisterham early in the narrative; described as asleep or stupefied.

characters.name: the Lascar
characters.description: Unnamed Lascar (sailor) in the opium den; present among the sleeping/drugged group.

characters.name: the haggard woman (opium den hostess)
characters.description: Unnamed haggard woman who runs the opium den; an opium-seller and hostess who tends customers in the early scene.
